newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to meet EMU convergence criteria - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Germany to meet EMU convergence criteria - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel insisted on Wednesday that Germany would meet convergence criteria for European monetary union (EMU) despite a likely delay to the transfer of profits from a revaluation of Bundesbank reserves.

"(Germany) will meet the three percent (public deficit-to-gross domestic product) criteria with additional efforts," Waigel told parliament, adding that Germany continued to demand a strict interpretation of the Maastricht criteria.

On the Bundesbank gold and currency reserves plan, Waigel said that the central bank itself would in any case have received the lion's share of any profits. He said its basic capital should be raised and its legally-allowed reserves should be increased to 100 percent of its capital.
Waigel said earlier he expected pay-outs from the revaluation to start in 1998 and not 1997, the year in which EMU qualification is based.
